title: Customer-class scheduling and fallback playbook
content:
Purpose
This note captures a concrete, implementation-first playbook for customer-class (tiered) request scheduling, backpressure, and graceful fallback across multi-region Redwood deployments. It is focused on operational controls the control plane must expose, the runtime policy enforcement points, and pragmatic runbook steps for incidents caused by noisy neighbors or cross-region failovers.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to request-time inference (hosted API + dedicated pockets). Not covering offline batch or embeddings cache priming.
- Customers are classified into classes (platinum, gold, standard, trial) using contract metadata surfaced in the control plane.
- We assume the system already has per-customer quotas and an identity mapping layer (org_id -> contract metadata).
- Goal: keep higher-tier SLAs stable while maximizing overall utilization and minimizing customer-visible errors.

High level approach
1) Classification + preflight: every request is annotated with customer_class, contract_slo, preemption_policy, and allowed_model_variants at the ingress.
2) Multi-layer enforcement: decisions occur at three layers: edge routing (region selection + capacity hints), queue-scheduling (priority + weighted fairness), and executor-level throttles (per-GPU admission control + KV cache throttles).
3) Graceful fallback: defined fallback chains per class (e.g., model-variant -> region -> degrade-mode) with explicit cost/latency tradeoffs and telemetry hooks.
4) Noise detection: track cross-tenant resource signals (GPU busy, KV cache hit rate drop, queue latency spike) and trigger tenant-specific mitigations (soft-throttle -> eviction -> fencing).

Key concepts and primitives
- customer_class: categorical label from contract (platinum/gold/standard/trial).
- hard_quota: contractual limit (tokens/sec or tokens/day) applied in control plane and enforced at runtime adapters.
- soft_budget: short-term credit derived from committed capacity buckets used by scheduler for short bursts.
- preemption_policy: whether higher-class traffic may preempt queued work from lower-class tenants (none | queue-preempt | executor-preempt).
- fallback_chain: ordered list of actions to try before returning an error to the client.
- tenant_fence_token: ephemeral token granting exclusive use of a portion of capacity when granted manually/automatically for mitigation.

Policy engine responsibilities
- Resolve customer_class and allowed_model_variants at ingress using contract metadata cache.
- Produce scheduling hints: priority weight, max_concurrency, burst_credits.
- Evaluate per-request fallback_chain and annotate the request for downstream enforcement.
- Emit audit event for any preemption or fallback decision for billing/product introspection.

Routing and multi-region rules (examples)
- Prefer local-region execution for a request if capacity_headroom >= 15% for requested model_family and customer_class != trial.
- If local headroom < 15%, route using this precedence: (region with headroom for same class) -> (region with headroom for any class but allowed by data residency) -> (degrade to smaller model_variant in local region) -> (return 503 with retry-after).
- Platinum contracts can specify geo-strict routing; default is "latency-priority then cost-priority".

Scheduler design (queue layer)
- Use a hybrid weighted fair queuing + priority shaper:
  - Each customer_class maps to a weight (platinum: 40, gold: 25, standard: 20, trial: 15).
  - Within a class, fairness uses a per-org deficit round robin keyed by org_id to avoid single-org monopolies in the same class.
  - Burst handling: soft_budget is decayed over a sliding window (60s) and can be drained when below threshold.
- Preemption options:
  - queue-preempt: allow a new high-priority request to jump ahead of the oldest queued low-priority request if queue latency for high class > configured_slo_latency.
  - executor-preempt: abort lower-priority in-flight non-critical requests (best-effort) when executor saturation threatens higher-tier SLAs. Requires idempotency and cancellation support.

Noisy neighbor detection and automated mitigations
- Signals we monitor per org_id: queue_wait_latency_p95, executor_cpu_utilization_p95, gpu_mem_pressure, kv_cache_hit_rate, error_rate_spike.
- Detection logic (example): mark noisy if any 3 of the following in 60s window: queue_wait_p95 > 2*SLO, gpu_mem_pressure > 85%, kv_cache_hit_rate drops by > 30%, sustained error spike > 4x baseline.
- Mitigation ladder (fast path automated):
  1) Soft-throttle at queue ingress (-20% throughput for offending org) and notify owner.
  2) Isolate KV cache partitions belonging to org (evict nonhot keys) for 30s.
  3) Apply tenant_fence_token granting exclusive, timebound mini-pool (if contract allows) OR evict to dedicated fallback (run on lower-priority nodes).
  4) If no improvement in 3 minutes -> circuit-break: reject new requests for org at fraction defined by contract (e.g., 50%).
- Manual escalation: on-call can request temporary dedicated capacity (if available) or permanently move offender to a dedicated pool if recurring.

SLA and billing interactions
- Every fallback/preemption event creates an audit record and optionally a usage adjustment for billing credit calculation.
- If a platinum contract requires "no-preempt" then preemption_policy must be set to none and control plane will reserve min_capacity in each region at allocation time. This affects admission control and autoscaler decisions.
- Billing-visible events: preemption, model-degrade, cross-region-fallback, tenant-fence activation. These are surfaced to billing pipeline with tags for invoice adjustments.

Example policy DSL snippet (pseudo-YAML)
  policy_id: plasma-2025-09
  match:
    - contract.class in ["platinum","gold"]
  actions:
    - set_priority: high
    - allow_preemption: queue-preempt
    - fallback_chain:
        - model_variant: smaller-fp16
        - remote_region: any-region-with-headroom
        - reply_error: 503-retry-after
  quotas:
    tokens_per_sec: "contract_limit"
    burst_budget_seconds: 60
  noisy_neighbor_rules:
    detection_window_secs: 60
    thresholds:
      queue_p95_ms: 2000
      gpu_mem_pct: 85
    auto_mitigations: [soft-throttle, kv-isolate, fence-or-evict]

Telemetry and SLOs to capture
- Per-org: request_rate, tokens/sec, q_latency_p50/p95/p99, model_latency_tail_p99, preempt_count, fallback_count, fence_activations.
- Per-region & model_family: capacity_headroom, queued_requests_by_class, executor_saturation.
- Alerting: when platinum class q_latency_p95 > SLA by 25% for 60s -> page SRE on-call.

Rollout and testing plan
- Phase 1 (canary config only): enable classification and auditing, but do not preempt or reroute. Validate mapping and telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (dark preemption): compute preemption decisions and log them; compare what would have happened vs actual for a week. Run replay tests against synthetic noisy tenants.
- Phase 3 (soft automated mitigations): enable soft-throttle + KV isolate on canary region for small % of traffic.
- Phase 4 (global rollout): enable full policy set with guardrails and kill switches.

Runbook excerpts (incident templates)
- Symptom: platinum requests latency spike and errors rising in primary region.
  1) Check capacity_headroom metric for region/model_family.
  2) Look at preemption and fallback audit log for last 5 minutes.
  3) If a noisy neighbor identified -> toggle soft-throttle for offender and watch q_latency_p95 for platinum.
  4) If no improvement within 2 minutes -> activate fallback to remote-region for affected platinum orgs and notify on-call.
- Symptom: KV cache hit-rate collapse for a subset of orgs.
  1) Identify top cache consumers by org_id.
  2) Evict ephemeral partitions for offender and enable kv-isolate.
  3) If root cause is abusive traffic, escalate to account team for rate-limiting or contract enforcement.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Preemption semantics for function/tool-calls: canceling in-flight calls can cause inconsistent downstream state. Need to mark cancellable request types explicitly.
- How to fairly price fallbacks and preemptions in billing while keeping product simple.
- Dedicated pools vs automatic fencing: does offering auto-fence reduce sales leverage for dedicated contracts? Need GTM input.

Next steps
- Implement ingress annotation endpoint and policy cache (owners: routing-engine). Track: JIRA-PLAT-987.
- Build dark-run harness for preemption decisions (routing-team + observability). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-engine/pull/412.
- Draft customer communication templates for any visible fallbacks (customer-success + legal).

Appendix: quick heuristics cheatsheet (for on-call)
- If region headroom < 10% and platinum q_p95 rising -> immediate region-prefetch: route <5% of platinum traffic to warm standby region.
- If single org owns >40% of class weight in a 1m window -> enforce per-org deficit-round-robin limit to 30% for that class until stable.
- Soft throttle levels: 10% -> 30% -> 50% applied over 30s steps.

End of playbook.
